clue.text: Cultivated member ate out

indicators.note: out says the word for ate sits on the outside, wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: ate means fed, as in 'we fed at noon'
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cultured club member who went to a restaurant for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like part of 'ate out' (dined at a restaurant), but here it says the word for 'ate' sits outside the limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Land that has been tilled and planted for crops has been cultivated, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Poor hearing, when one is in the wind

indicators.note: is in tells us the numeral for one is placed inside the name of the wind

parts.note: the mistral is a cold northerly wind in southern France
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A complaint that a court hearing went badly because someone was swept up in a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like the sense of listening; here it is a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial invalidated by an error is a botched legal hearing, so a poor one.

clue.text: All-out extremely tight sumo wrestling

indicators.note: wrestling suggests bodies twisting and grappling, so these letters are thrown into a new order
extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of the word tight

explanation.surface: A description of sumo wrestlers grappling at full stretch in a tight bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'tight' but gives its outer letters TT, which are mixed with SUMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving one's maximum effort is an all-out effort, the greatest possible degree.

clue.text: Leaves to set up taxi firm

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for taxi is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
Co is the standard abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone departs in order to start up a taxi company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (departs) but is the noun: dried leaves for smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: The cured foliage of the plant is smoked or chewed, so the product is literally leaves.

clue.text: Then compete and start to turn red

parts.note: so can mean then, as in 'so we left'
to vie is to compete

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Instructions in a game: then compete, and begin to change colour to red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like a colour but is the old political label for a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Communists were called reds, and the USSR was the communist state, so its citizens were reds.

clue.text: Fiendish foxtrot gives way to tango from within

indicators.note: gives way to means the first letter yields its place, being replaced by the second

parts.note: infernal means hellish, fiendish
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ballroom dance report: a devilishly hard foxtrot is replaced by a tango from inside the hall.
explanation.walkthrough: The dances are not dances: Foxtrot and Tango are the radio alphabet's F and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arising from inside, as in an internal inquiry, comes from within.

clue.text: Help turned into helping waves

indicators.note: into means the turned piece is put inside the word for helping

parts.note: a ration is a portion, a helping of food

indicators.note: turned means the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help

explanation.surface: Help that became a helping, then waves: a strange story of charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy travelling as electromagnetic waves, such as light or X-rays, is radiation.

clue.text: Channel something heard well

definitions.meaning: a strait, a narrow sea channel, as in Puget's
a noise, anything that reaches the ear
healthy, in good condition, as in 'of whole mind and body'

explanation.definitionFit: Three senses of one word: a sea strait, a noise, and healthy or solid.

clue.text: A moonlit romance ultimately makes one thus

definitions.text: A moonlit romance ultimately makes one thus

indicators.note: ultimately means take the final letter of romance
makes is taken as 'makes into', remaking the letters of a moonlit into a new order

explanation.surface: A moonlit romance leaves a person moved and full of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a moonlit romance would leave anyone feeling this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stirred by strong feelings, as moonlit love affairs make people, is being emotional.

clue.text: Declared 48 hours before D-day, what makes privates presentable

indicators.note: declared means the phrase is spoken, so we take its pronunciation

parts.note: two days before day D, counting back through the alphabet, is day B, said 'bee day'

explanation.surface: A military announcement made two days before an invasion, with a punchline about private soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'privates' looks like soldiers but means private parts. In French the word is said 'bee-day', which is how 'B-day' sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A low basin for washing one's genitals cleans the private parts, making them fit to be seen.

clue.text: See 16
Going nowhere in commercial break

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A TV ad break seems to go on and on, getting nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial break' reads as one phrase, an ad slot, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat floating aimlessly is going nowhere in particular, without direction.

clue.text: Those against accepting defeat are in the soup

indicators.note: accepting means the word for those against takes in the other piece

parts.note: the cons are those arguing against, as in pros and cons
a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: Opponents who concede defeat are in trouble, in the soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble, but literally means floating in soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Small fried bread cubes are a common garnish that sit in soup.

clue.text: Some Laurel and Hardy finally in a fable that's been rewritten

indicators.note: in means the last letter of the comedian's name goes inside the rearranged letters
rewritten means the letters of a fable are written out again in a different order
finally means take the last letter of Hardy

explanation.surface: Laurel and Hardy appear in a fable that has been rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laurel and Hardy' suggests the comedy duo, but Laurel is the tree and Hardy only gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The laurel tree is also called bay, so one of its leaves is part of the laurel.

clue.text: A dreamer with no name is fragrant

indicators.note: with no means the letter for name is removed from the dreamer

parts.note: a romantic is an idealist, a dreamer

explanation.surface: An anonymous dreamer smells sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving off a pleasant, spicy smell is a synonym for being fragrant.

clue.text: Fancy diet not a cure

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or fanciful, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trendy diet is not a cure-all, says a sceptic.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy that counteracts a poison or problem is a cure in a broad sense.

clue.text: Decide about a city in the US

indicators.note: about means the word for decide goes round the letter a

parts.note: to settle a matter is to decide it

explanation.surface: Someone decides where to move: a city somewhere in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city in Washington state is an example of a US city.

clue.text: Credit slip uncovered: don't say a word — it's sensitive

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters of slip are stripped away

parts.note: sh is the call for silence, telling someone not to speak

explanation.surface: A shameful credit slip is exposed: keep quiet about it, it's a delicate matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Buying 'on tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicate or touchy matter is a sensitive one, needing careful handling.

clue.text: Sun now, then rain

parts.note: if it is Sunday now, then the next day, Monday, comes soon; and the whole is a season of heavy rain

explanation.surface: A weather forecast: sunshine now, then rain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' is not sunshine but Sunday: if it is Sun now, then MON is SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: The seasonal wind of South Asia brings torrential rain after hot sunny spells.

clue.text: The next sound as well is a bird

indicators.note: sound tells us to take how the next answer is pronounced, not how it is written

parts.note: points to the following clue's answer, 22-across, a breed of spaniel
too means as well, also

explanation.surface: The next noise you hear, too, is a bird's call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The next' refers to the answer to the following clue, 22 across, said aloud as non-rhotic British speech says it.
explanation.definitionFit: The crested parrot of Australia is a particular kind of bird.

clue.text: 18 not 51, may be vulgar

indicators.note: may be suggests what the remaining letters could become, rearranged
not means the letters for 51 are left out

parts.note: 18 refers to the answer to 18-down
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A cryptic sentence of numbers: eighteen without fifty-one may be crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Take LI from 18-down's answer to leave TICKSH; 'may be' then rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Garish, tasteless art or decor is often called vulgar, the core sense of the German loanword.

clue.text: Small dog locker with doubled top

indicators.note: the letter C already in the word is doubled up to take the place of the top letter L

explanation.surface: A puppy is kept in a locker with a double lid on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with doubled top' replaces the L at the top of LOCKER with a second C, the letter already in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocker spaniel is the smallest of the sporting spaniels, a small dog breed.

clue.text: Harsh lectures to the audience

indicators.note: to the audience means as heard by listeners, so we take how the word is pronounced

parts.note: a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: Someone delivers harsh lectures to the people listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough and crude in texture or manner, coarse means harsh.

clue.text: Evenly and softly to begin with, that's right: not so hard

indicators.note: to begin with means take the first letters of the three words before it

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Instructions: steadily and gently at first, that's right, it's getting less difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evenly' looks like an alternate-letters signal, but it only gives its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being less difficult is the comparative of easy, the opposite of harder.

clue.text: Start off continent expedition

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: continent, as an adjective, means sexually restrained, chaste

explanation.surface: An expedition sets off from a continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'continent' looks like a landmass but is the adjective meaning self-restrained. 'expedition' is used in its old sense of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed of action, so hurry is a synonym.

clue.text: What covers essay by learner is found

indicators.note: covers means the exclamation goes round the other pieces

parts.note: eish is a South African exclamation of surprise, like 'what!'
an essay is an attempt, a stab
L is the learner sign on a car

explanation.surface: Someone asks what covers an essay written by a student who has been found out.
explanation.walkthrough: EISH is South African slang for a startled 'what!'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set up an institution is to found it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Flinch from overflow in cesspit

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are drawn out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at an overflowing cesspit.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil or grimace in sudden pain or disgust is to flinch.

clue.text: Had search party status evaluated externally

parts.note: a posse is a group gathered to hunt someone down

indicators.note: externally means take the outer letters of status and of evaluated

explanation.surface: A search party had its standing assessed by an outside reviewer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to own it, so had means owned.
